Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement and Legal have a short set of questions we need answered as part of our RFP on regional availability and data location controls. Please see inline questions below and attach any diagrams/policy docs you can share. We need responses by EOD Monday.

1) In which cloud regions do you host customer data for the hosted API (list by cloud provider and region)?
2) Can customers require that all persistent data (logs, traces, persisted artifacts) for a given tenant remain physically in the EU? If so, how is that enforced?
3) Do any model training/update pipelines access customer data in a different region for model improvement?
4) What encryption at rest/key management options are available (Redwood-managed KMS, customer-managed keys, HSM)?
4a) If customer-managed KMS, can you describe the workflow for key rotation and revocation?
5) For customers on Dedicated or Private deployments, what network controls are supported (VPC peering, private endpoints, air-gapped on-prem)?
6) Do you provide audit log exports and for how long are logs retained in hosted plans by default?
7) Any contractual data residency guarantees that are part of a Dedicated/Private agreement?

Appreciate concise answers and any attachments that map regions to product features.

Best,
Alice

Hi Alice — thanks for the list. See answers below (high level) and I attached a region matrix and KMS diagram. Happy to expand any item.

1) Hosted API regions: We operate hosted endpoints in multiple cloud regions across AWS, GCP, and Azure. For the EU we currently offer: AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), GCP (europe-west1, europe-west2), Azure (West Europe, North Europe). Full provider/region map attached (region_matrix_v1.xlsx).

2) EU-only persistent data: Yes — for customers requiring EU-only residency we provide two options:
  - Hosted with regional routing + soft isolation: all persistent artifacts (usage logs, model traces) are written to storage in the selected EU region and routed to EU compute. This is enforced by our smart-routing policy and separate region-specific storage buckets.
  - Dedicated/Private deployment: for contractual guarantees we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity in an EU region) or Private (VPC or on-prem) which provide stronger contractual residency guarantees (see Q7).

3) Model training/updates: Our hosted model improvement pipelines do not ingest customer prompt-level content by default. Customers can opt-in. For customers with EU residency requirements, model updates can be performed inside the EU for opted-in telemetry; for Dedicated/Private customers, telemetry for model improvement never leaves the deployed region unless explicitly agreed.

4) Encryption & KMS: We support Redwood-managed keys (default), customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and HSM integrations for Private deployments.

4a) Customer-managed KMS workflow: Customers provide a key ARN/URL and grant Redwood a limited-use role to wrap/unwrap encryption operations. Key rotation is performed by the customer; Redwood supports rekeying by fetching the new key metadata and re-wrapping existing data keys without moving data. Revocation: if customer revokes access, Redwood will stop being able to decrypt new requests; for Dedicated/Private we provide a maintenance path to export data or place instances into an emergency maintenance mode. Diagram attached (kms_integration_diagram.pdf).

5) Network controls: Dedicated supports VPC peering, PrivateLink (AWS) / Private Endpoint equivalents, customer-managed NAT/proxy for egress filtering. Private deployments can be delivered as a customer-managed VPC or an on-prem appliance (air-gapped) depending on procurement.

6) Audit logs & retention: Hosted default retention is 90 days for high-level request logs and 30 days for raw token-level traces; exports can be configured and shipped to customer-owned S3/GCS/Azure Blob for longer retention. Dedicated/Private include configurable retention as part of the contract.

7) Contractual guarantees: We offer data residency and location covenants in Dedicated and Private contracts (we will add an EU-only residency clause and can include audit rights, breach notification timing, and data deletion SLAs).

Attachments: region_matrix_v1.xlsx, kms_integration_diagram.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Let me know if you want a short call to walk through the matrix — happy to set one up with Markus (product/security) and Lauren (legal).

Hi Alice — agreed and understood. Draft clause below you can drop into your redlines; I also confirm third-party processors and monitoring endpoints for our hosted EU routing are restricted to providers with EU-region data processing agreements (we use EU-based logging endpoints for EU-routed tenants). For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide full list and add a contractual restriction on processors.

Draft clause (suggested):
"Redwood Inference will store and process Customer Data for the Customer's EU-routed deployment exclusively within the European Union unless the Customer provides explicit, documented consent to transfer or unless such transfer is required for emergency maintenance that cannot be performed within the EU. Redwood will notify Customer no less than 72 hours prior to any planned transfer and will provide details of the scope and duration of such transfer. Redwood will ensure that any third-party subprocessors engaged to provide monitoring or logging services for EU-routed Customer Data are contractually bound to process such data within the EU and comply with applicable data protection laws."

Operational notes: we typically use EU-region logging pipelines (ELK/GCP logging in EU), and our monitoring vendor contracts include EU processing commitments for EU tenants. For Dedicated engagements we can exclude specific subprocessors by agreement.

Next steps: I can attach a short SOC2 supplement and a proposed contractual residency addendum. Would you like us to open a DocuSign for a redline with your Legal?

Thanks,
Soojin
